profiles.name: Van Alen Institute
profiles.desc: Van Alen Institute at 303 Bond Street in Gowanus. What it does, how to reach it, and the lot it stands on. Brooklyn Community Board 6 holds its meetings there.
profiles.addr_note: Between Union and Sackett Streets, on the west bank of the canal
intro: The Van Alen Institute has been at this since 1894, which makes it older than the Gowanus rezoning by about a century and a quarter. It works on community-led urban design, the premise being that the people who live somewhere know things about it that a designer parachuting in does not.

What that means in practice is that it builds coalitions across designers, residents and city agencies, then backs them with scoping, hands-on guidance and seed money. It is explicit that its work is about power imbalances in how cities get made, and it partners with historically disinvested communities rather than the ones already well served.

It moved to 303 Bond Street in Gowanus, on the west bank of the canal, inside the area the 2021 rezoning reshaped. Brooklyn Community Board 6 holds our meetings there, which is a good arrangement for everyone: an organisation devoted to community-led design hosting the body whose whole job is community input on land use.
does: Van Alen runs design competitions, public space projects, research and fellowships. The through line is that it does not just publish a report and leave; it puts money and staff behind the ideas it generates and stays with them.

For CB6 the relevant thing is proximity and subject matter. This is a district with a Superfund canal, a major rezoning still being built out, a waterfront terminal decision coming, and six historic districts. An institution working on how communities shape the built environment is useful to have on the block.
kv: Brooklyn Community Board 6 holds its meetings here

profiles.name: Gowanus Canal Conservancy
profiles.desc: Gowanus Canal Conservancy at the Old American Can Factory, 248 Third Street. Stewardship of the canal watershed, the Lowlands Nursery, the Green Team and the Tree Network.
profiles.addr: The Old American Can Factory, 248 Third Street
profiles.addr_note: Third Street at Third Avenue. The city files the lot as 361 3 Avenue
intro: The Gowanus Canal Conservancy is the group that has done the work on the canal since 2006, out of the Old American Can Factory: volunteers in the rain gardens and tree pits, students in the watershed, and staff at every meeting where the canal’s future gets decided, including ours. On the rezoning they were ahead of everyone, with a plan for the waterfront before the City had one, and they’re on the Oversight Task Force now making sure the open space and stormwater commitments get built.

Andrea Parker and her excellent team has run and met the moment for over a decade, and her team includes CB6 member Aurelia Casey. If you want to see what stewardship looks like in practice, go to the Salt Lot on a volunteer day.
does: GCC runs the Lowlands Nursery, growing native urban-adapted plants and selling them to residents, institutions and landscape designers, with proceeds going back into education and stewardship.

GCC runs the Gowanus Green Team, paid high school apprentices doing conservation work, and the Gowanus Tree Network, which trains neighbours as Citizen Pruners to look after the street trees on their own blocks.

The Conservancy works out of the Old American Can Factory, a three storey 1890 complex at Third Street and Third Avenue that now houses artists, makers and non-profits. The lot is zoned M1-4/R7X inside the Gowanus special district, the mixed use zoning the 2021 rezoning brought in.

profiles.name: Park Slope Food Coop
profiles.seat: Member-owned food cooperative · Park Slope, Brooklyn
profiles.desc: Park Slope Food Coop at 782 Union Street. A member-owned and member-run grocery since 1973: hours, how it works, the monthly General Meeting, and the lot it stands on.
profiles.addr_note: Between Sixth and Seventh Avenues. The city files the lot as 780 Union Street
intro: The Park Slope Food Coop has been at 782 Union Street since 1973. Members own the store and run it: every member works a shift, only members shop, and the labor is what keeps the prices down. The monthly General Meeting, open to every member with a vote for everyone who shows up, has been the decision-making body from the start.

The Coop is one of the oldest and largest member-run food cooperatives in the country, and it is a Park Slope institution in the plainest sense: a two storey building on a residential block that thousands of households pass through every week.
does: The Coop is a member-owned and operated food store. Membership is open to all, only members may shop, and members contribute their labor on recurring work shifts, sharing the responsibilities and the benefits equally. The store buys as an agent for its members, with an emphasis on organic, minimally processed food and local, earth-friendly producers.

The General Meeting is held on the last Tuesday of each month at 7 PM. The agenda, with the location and how to attend, is posted inside the Coop and online about three weeks ahead. The Board of Directors is elected at the Annual Meeting in June.
The building at 782 Union Street is a two storey store built in 1920 on a 7,980 square foot lot, owned by the Coop itself. The lot is zoned R6A.

profiles.name: Fifth Avenue Committee
profiles.seat: Community based organisation · Park Slope and Gowanus, Brooklyn
profiles.desc: Fifth Avenue Committee at 621 DeGraw Street. Affordable housing, organizing, adult education and workforce development since 1978.
profiles.addr_note: Second office at 132 32nd Street, Suite 106, Brooklyn, NY 11232
intro: The Fifth Avenue Committee has been at this since 1978, and it is one of the few organisations in the district that does development, organizing and services at the same time rather than picking one. It reaches more than 6,500 low and moderate income New Yorkers a year.

Its stated aim is economic, social and racial justice, pursued through community-centred affordable housing, grassroots organizing, policy advocacy, and education and training. That combination is the point. An organisation that only builds housing does not have tenants organized; one that only organizes does not own anything.
The lot at 621 DeGraw is owned by FAC Center Local Development Corporation, which tells you something. They own the building they organize from.
does: On housing it builds and manages affordable and supportive housing, with a pipeline running to as many as 1,900 units, and it has done the unglamorous work too: gut renovations of small rental buildings, LEED Gold mixed-income developments, and a public library, a public park and five Pre-K classrooms folded into its projects.

On the ground it runs tenant counseling and organizing, foreclosure prevention and homebuyer counseling, and adult education including GED prep, English classes and digital literacy for over a thousand adults a year.
Workforce development runs through its affiliate Brooklyn Workforce Innovations. South Brooklyn Against Displacement is its organizing arm.

profiles.name: The Old Stone House
profiles.seat: Historic house and Washington Park · Park Slope and Gowanus, Brooklyn
profiles.desc: The Old Stone House at 336 3rd Street in Washington Park. What it runs, how to reach it, and the ground it stands on.
profiles.addr_note: Between 4th and 5th Avenues, inside Washington Park
intro: The Old Stone House sits where history actually happened, in the middle of Washington Park, between 3rd and 4th Streets and between 4th and 5th Avenues. It runs family programs, arts and cultural events, addresses neighborhood issues, and manages the gardens; aka it’s a great institution.

A house that has grown by leaps and bounds in the decades since I was in middle school in the late 1990s. Much of that is down to Executive Director Kim Maier, who has built it into a place that honors the past, lives in the present, and improves the future.

The building, the actual house, is a reconstruction of the 1699 Vechte-Cortelyou House, on land taken from the Lenape as early as 1639. It stands in Washington Park on the border of Park Slope and Gowanus, marking the site of the original Dutch farmstead and the culminating engagement of the Battle of Brooklyn in 1776. It is also the birthplace of the Brooklyn Dodgers back when there were trolley’s to dodge. It is a Historic House Trust of New York City site and rightly resides on the National Register of Historic Places.
does: An interactive exhibit on the largest battle of the Revolutionary War and what living in Brooklyn was like from 1776 to 1783. Contemporary shows by emerging artists. Gardens of native and useful plants. School visits and field trips. Concerts, readings, lectures and theater, including Piper Theatre. A summer camp. And the playground, courts, turf field and dog run that make up JJ Byrne.

profiles.name: Arts Gowanus
profiles.seat: Community based arts organisation · Gowanus, Brooklyn
profiles.desc: Arts Gowanus at 543 Union Street in Gowanus. Gowanus Open Studios, art programming, the Arts Gowanus Fellowship, and advocacy for affordable artist studios in the Gowanus rezoning.
intro: Arts Gowanus has worked for the artists of Gowanus since 1996. In the words of its own mission, Arts Gowanus nurtures a diverse, inclusive creative community that welcomes all artists in the neighborhood, creating new spaces for art to bring people together, build a more vibrant community, and uplift the greater Gowanus area.

Arts Gowanus runs Gowanus Open Studios, which it calls Brooklyn’s largest celebration of local art, with more than 400 artists, businesses and venues opening their doors from Pacific Street to 19th Street and from Smith Street to Fifth Avenue. The 30th annual Open Studios is October 17 and 18, 2026.
Executive Director Johnny Thornton leads the organisation.
does: Arts Gowanus runs art programming and partnerships that raise the visibility of Gowanus artists across the city, the Arts Gowanus Fellowship, which covers a selected artist’s studio rent, and curatorial services.

On the Gowanus rezoning, Arts Gowanus negotiated a Community Benefits Agreement that secures roughly 120 subsidized artist studios across the development sites, starting at $20 a square foot a year, with one studio in each building reserved for a low income artist. The agreement also secures a 2,000 square foot community arts center with three residency studios, affordable in perpetuity.

Arts Gowanus works alongside the Gowanus Neighborhood Coalition for Justice, the Gowanus Oversight Task Force, GRACE and the Gowanus Improvement District. The office at 543 Union Street is zoned M1-4/R7-2 inside the Gowanus special district.

going.title: David Briggs at Threes Brewing
going.text: The Threes Brewing curatorial partnership, the quarterly series Arts Gowanus curates at Threes Brewing, 333 Douglass Street, shows work by David Briggs, an architect, artist and community activist in Brooklyn.

going.title: Subsidized artist studios
going.text: Between 100 and 140 subsidized artist studios, about 130 to 350 square feet each, are coming to the Gowanus development sites under the Arts Gowanus Community Benefits Agreement. Rent starts at $20 a square foot a year, about $332 a month for 200 square feet. Applying through Arts Gowanus is the only way to lease one, and applications are taken on a rolling basis.

profiles.name: SBIDC
profiles.seat: Southwest Brooklyn Industrial Development Corporation · Sunset Park, Red Hook and Gowanus
profiles.desc: SBIDC, the Southwest Brooklyn Industrial Development Corporation, at 4223 1st Avenue. Business support and training, green economy, employee ownership, workforce services and advocacy for the Southwest Brooklyn industrial waterfront since 1978.
intro: SBIDC, the Southwest Brooklyn Industrial Development Corporation, has been creating opportunity in Southwest Brooklyn since 1978. In the words of its own mission, SBIDC is a resource that creates equal opportunity for the people, businesses and community of the Southwest Brooklyn industrial waterfront.
SBIDC serves the waterfront neighborhoods of Sunset Park, Red Hook and Gowanus, two of them in CB6.
Executive Director Jesse Tinen Solomon leads the organisation.
does: For businesses, SBIDC offers business support, business training, green economy programs and help with employee ownership.
For workers, SBIDC runs workforce services, job placement and skill development, through the Sunset Park Economic Mobility Network.
SBIDC also provides advocacy support, representing the industrial business community.
